The Ring That Will Not Close

The Ring That Will Not Close

Twelve voices on a ring. Each is told one thing: be a pure fifth above the voice to your left. Around the ring that is impossible by 23.46 cents, the Pythagorean comma, so the error has to live somewhere. You hear the ring one fifth at a time, as a tuner would. Push a voice, pin a voice, change what the ring minds about, and listen to where the comma goes.

What the ring minds

Sensory roughness (Sethares) of this timbre at this register, computed from the same six-harmonic tone you are hearing. It has a sharp V at the pure fifth and flattens outward: small errors cost almost as much as big ones.

How the voices listen

each follows its right neighbourmutualeach follows its left

Off: every fifth relaxes all the time. On: nothing moves except the sounding pair, and λ decides which of its two voices gives way. A dwell of about 2 s lets the tuner finish; a hurried tuner (short dwell) leaves the job half done and the comma smears.

Set the ring

Drag a voice up or down to push its pitch. Tap a voice to pin it (it stops listening). Pins are shown as rings.

What to try
  1. Hear the wolf. Turn sound on. The ring starts with eleven pure fifths and one wolf. Let the window go round once. Pure fifths are still; the wolf beats.
  2. Forgetting and remembering. With Quadratic, press Equal temperament, then drag any voice 20 cents and let go: the ring returns to equal temperament every time. Switch to Roughness and do the same: the comma stays, as a wolf, wherever your push left it.
  3. Equal temperament falls apart. With Roughness, press Equal temperament and wait. Twelve slightly flat fifths condense into one wolf in under a minute, on an edge the noise picks. Press again; it picks a different edge.
  4. Drift without transport. Set λ fully to one side (each voice follows one neighbour). The whole ring slides in pitch, several cents a second, and the wolf stays exactly where it was.
  5. The tuner's shadow. Turn on Tuner mode with λ at follows its left and the window moving up the ring. Every fifth you arrive at is the wolf; you tune it pure, and it is waiting on the next one. Set λ to mutual instead and go round several times: the tuner equal-tempers the ring by halves.
  6. The control. Switch to All twelve at once. Now try to say where the wolf is.
The rules, exactly

Pitch classes θ₀…θ₁₁ in cents. The error on edge i is the fifth's mistuning:

ε_i = wrap(θ_{i+1} − θ_i − 701.955)            wrap into (−600, 600]
Σ ε_i = −23.46 + 1200·k                          always; k is a winding number

θ̇_i = R · [ (1−λ)·g_i·F(ε_i) − λ·g_{i−1}·F(ε_{i−1}) ]
F = D′, the slope of the chosen discomfort curve D
λ = ½  mutual (gradient descent on Σ D(ε_i));  λ = 1  each voice follows its left neighbour;  λ = 0  its right
g_i = 1,  or in tuner mode  g_i = 3 on the sounding edge and 0 elsewhere
pinned voices: θ̇_i = 0.   noise: + σ·√dt·N(0,1) per voice per sub-step (σ shown above; set it to 0)

Quadratic: D = ε²/2, F = ε. Roughness: Sethares sensory dissonance of two six-harmonic tones (amplitudes 0.88ᵏ⁻¹) for a lower voice at the middle of the chosen octave, as a function of the fifth's mistuning, over the whole sector; smoothed with σ = 0.5 cents so the V at the pure fifth has finite stiffness; F normalised so max|F| within ±60 cents is 12. The same curve is used on every edge (the true curve varies a little with the lower voice's frequency within the octave; that variation is dropped).

Integration: explicit Euler, 4 ms sub-steps, 2-cent cap per sub-step. There are no other rules, no special cases, and nothing scripted. Everything you hear and see follows from the lines above; the full source is in the page.
